title: Yisroel and Yaakov: the middle line, emes and daas
overview: Chapter 35 explains *Yisroel* and *Yaakov* as two levels of the middos of *Zeir Anpin*. *Yaakov* is the middos in *katnus*, G-dliness hidden in nature; *Yisroel* is the same middos in *gadlus*, when a person's G-dly soul is revealed and rules over nature. *Yaakov* is the middle line, which joins *chesed* and *gevura* and runs unbroken from top to bottom, like the beam through the walls of the *Mishkan*. The right and left lines are not joined this way: *chachma* does not go straight into *chesed*, and *netzach* and *hod* lose the light of the *mochin*, so their actions turn dry and lose their reason. Without a connection to the top, *chesed* goes down into *Yishmael* and *gevura* into *Esav*. *Daas* is the inner part of *rachamim*: a person without *daas* is cruel, and the more *daas* he has, the more mercy he feels. Because the middle line stays connected, even a sincere person on a low level is plugged into the truth. *Yaakov* did not die, because the *kelipa* cannot grip the middle line. The chapter ends with the *geulah*: a Jew's soul is never in *galus*, and the inner *shtus d'kedusha* brings the *geulah* even to the outer.

sections.title: Yisroel: the light of Keser ruling over chachma
sections.summary: *Yisroel* is the level where a person's G-dly soul is revealed and rules over nature. In *Kabbalah* the name also means that the light of *Keser* shines into *chachma* and rules over it.

phrases.en: this is the level of *Yisroel*
that it's ruling over *kel*

phrases.he: דהיינו על ידי הארת הכתר בחכמה
phrases.en: there's the light of *Keser* that's shining into *Chochma*
this is the *kel*, which is the light of *Chochma*
that *Keser* is ruling over *Chochma*

phrases.he: כו' כמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין כי שרית וכו':

blocks.text: The chapter goes on with the levels of *Zeir Anpin*: *Yisroel* and *Yaakov*. To understand them one needs *katnus* and *gadlus*, smallness and maturity, the way a child grows up. When G-dliness is hidden in nature, that is *katnus*. When a person sees that G-d transcends nature, as in miracles, that is *gadlus*. So in general *Yaakov* is the middos of *Zeir Anpin* in *katnus*, and *Yisroel* is the same middos in *gadlus*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Opening of the class, before line 1 is read: he explains *katnus* and *gadlus* first, on which the reading rests.

blocks.text: *Yisroel* has a meaning beyond the simple one of a Jew. In *Kabbalah*, and in Jewish literature in general, it names a person whose G-dly soul is revealed. So the *Rambam* says that when a person reveals his G-dly soul by understanding and believing the thirteen principles of faith, the thirteen *ani ma'amin*, he is called a *Yisroel*.

The simple meaning is *sar kel*, ruling over *kel*: *Yaakov* was named *Yisroel* after he beat *Esav*'s angel, because he ruled over angels and men. In *Kabbalah* it means the light of *Keser* shining into *chachma* and ruling it; *kel* is *chachma*.

This is the recognition that a person has something higher than what he understands. In the previous chapter he spoke of a person who reaches twenty and reveals the middos of *Keser*, and can change what he wants, on the level of *ratzon* and *taanug*. That is the idea of a *tzaddik*, though every person can have some of it. In the *sefiros* it is the recognition that G-d dictates the logic of reality, so He is not bound by it.

*Kel* is the light of *chachma*, and its ruler, the *sar kel*, is *Keser*, as is explained elsewhere. Why are the angels called *kel*? Because their names contain it: it means a power or a force. *Raphael* is the healing power of G-d, *Michael* the power of kindness, *Gavriel* the power of justice, as opposed to human justice. All the forces that create and run nature are called these angels.
*Elokim* is the name of G-d for nature, the master of the forces, a judge in charge of a system. Like *kel* in the plural, the all-powerful.

So *Yisroel* is a person who conquers his nature. *Yaakov* was timid, worried about *Esav*, and he overcame his nature and did what was beyond it. That is the maturity not to be trapped by nature, whether the animal soul's or even the G-dly soul's, to go beyond it, accept the yoke and give self-sacrifice.

blocks.question: Is there any truth to the reading that *Yisroel* means struggling with G-d?
blocks.text: Torah has many interpretations. He does not know where this one comes from; the test is whether it helps your *avodas Hashem*. There can be truth in the struggle reading, but it is not the simple one: by *Rashi* and the verse, *Yaakov* struggled with an angel and beat him, and ruled over men and angels. Still, if a person feels he struggles with his faith, it is healthy to be at ease with that: I'm human, I have a struggle, and that's okay. I don't have to beat myself up. I just keep going.

sections.title: Yisroel and Leah, Yaakov and Rachel: unions of the middos
sections.summary: The *partzufim* of *Zeir Anpin* and *Malchus* are named after *Yisroel*, *Yaakov*, *Leah* and *Rachel*. Each union is of the middos with thought or with speech, and the difference between *Yisroel* and *Yaakov* has to come first.

phrases.en: so now we need to understand
the idea of the union of *Yisroel* and *Leah*

phrases.he: שהוא יחוד המדות במחשבה שנקרא לאה,
phrases.en: that's the way the middos unite with thought, which is *Leah*

phrases.he: ויחוד יעקב ורחל, שהוא יחוד המדות בדבור
phrases.en: the way the emotions unite with speech, when a person expresses their feeling in their words

blocks.text: Union is a big idea in *Kabbalah*, often described with the metaphor of marriage and intimacy. *Zeir Anpin* has configurations called *partzufim*, faces, named after *Yisroel*, *Yaakov* and the like. *Nukva*, which is *Malchus*, is also viewed as a face, and in a face each *sefira* contains all ten *sefiros*.
In *tohu* the *sefiros* were separate. In *tikun* each has all ten inside it, so the lights of *chesed* can enter the vessels of *gevura*. Developed that way, with all ten, it is a *partzuf*.

In *Malchus* the faces are named after figures too, such as *Leah* and *Rachel*, *Yaakov*'s two wives. *Bilhah* and *Zilpah* he leaves for elsewhere. These are different ways *Zeir Anpin* and *Malchus* can come together.

The union of *Yisroel* and *Leah* is the union of the middos, in their maturity, with thought. The union of *Yaakov* and *Rachel* is the union of the less mature middos with speech: the person expresses his feeling in words. He introduces both here and explains them later.

phrases.he: ותחלה יש להבין בהפרש שבין ישראל ליעקב
phrases.en: first we have to understand better this difference between *Yisroel* and *Yaakov*

blocks.text: The *Mitteler Rebbe* follows his usual method: he first names the concept he will explain, then gives its basic idea and metaphors. Here he only names the unions. He thinks the right place to take it up is chapter 37, because this chapter explains *Yisroel* and *Yaakov* first, and the next chapter explains *Yosef*. So first one must understand the difference between *Yisroel* and *Yaakov*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Said before line 4 is read: he says the unions themselves are taken up in chapter 37.

sections.title: Yaakov is tiferes, the mercy that unites opposites
sections.summary: *Yaakov* is the *tiferes* of *Zeir Anpin*, where the middos join. Mercy combines *chesed* and *gevura*, and truth too is seeing both sides and uniting them.

phrases.he: דהנה בחינת יעקב הוא בחינת תפארת דזעיר אנפין דאצילות וכו',
phrases.en: that *Yaakov* represents this *partzuf*, each one focused on a certain *sefira*
*Yaakov* is focused on *tiferes* of *Zeir Anpin*, the way all the middos of *Zeir Anpin* unite, which is the attribute of mercy
as is known
that the forefathers represent the divine chariot
*Avraham* represented, his life was expressing G-d's, the g-dly kindness
*Yitzchak* was expressing g-dly *gevura* of determination
and *Yaakov* was *tiferes* of this idea of mercy

phrases.he: וכתיב תתן אמת ליעקב, חסד לאברהם כו'
phrases.en: we also find that *Yaakov* is associated with truth, like it says, give truth to *Yaakov* and kindness to *Avraham*

blocks.text: *Yaakov* is the *tiferes* of *Zeir Anpin*, where its middos unite: the middah of mercy. Each *partzuf* is focused on one *sefira*.

The forefathers are the divine chariot, and each was a vehicle for one of the middos of *Zeir Anpin*. *Avraham* expressed *chesed*, and his life was the G-dly kindness. *Yitzchak* expressed the *gevura* of determination. *Yaakov* expressed the *tiferes* of mercy.

Truth is given to *Yaakov*, kindness to *Avraham*. *Tiferes*, mercy, combines *chesed*, which gives to all, and *gevura*, which gives only to the deserving. Mercy helps the poor who do not deserve it, and tells the rich to work for it.

This mercy sees the gap between a person's potential and how low he actually is, and that recognition produces mercy. Truth is also seeing both sides of an argument, and finding some truth in each rather than taking one side. So the main idea of *tiferes* is uniting opposites, and it shows up in these different ways.

sections.title: The middle line balances chesed and gevura, and truth is what endures
sections.summary: *Yaakov* is the middle line, the *vav* of *emes*. Right and left oppose each other, and *chesed* and *din* limit each other. Truth is what endures, because it holds both sides together.

phrases.en: it says in the *Zohar*

phrases.he: על פסוק ונתתם לי אות אמת,
phrases.en: that you've given me a sign of truth; it translates the word *ot* as a letter, a letter of truth
that's the letter *vav*
that represents *Yaakov*, who is the middle line
that's called the *briach hatichon*, the support beam

blocks.text: The *Zohar* says the letter of truth is the letter *vav*, which stands for *Yaakov*, the middle line. The *sefiros* have a right line, *chachma*, *chesed*, *netzach*, and a left line, *bina*, *gevura*, *hod*. The middle line is *Keser*, *Daas*, *Tiferes*, *Yesod*, *Malchus*, and it is called the *briach hatichon*, the support beam.

blocks.title: The bar through the walls of the *Mishkan*
blocks.text: Think of the beams of the *Mishkan*. Each beam had rings of wood at the top and bottom that held the walls, and in the middle a hole was bored straight through the beam. One long piece of wood went through the middle of all of them, all the way around the three walls. So the right and left *sefiros* do not fully connect: *chachma* does not connect directly to *chesed*. But the middle *sefiros* are really one *sefira* that extends lower and lower. That is the *briach hatichon*.

phrases.he: והענין ידוע דקו הימין חח''ן, הרי קו השמאל בג''ה סותרו
phrases.en: the idea is known, that the right line is opposed by the left line

phrases.he: כמו שמדת הדין סותר למדת החסד ומגביל אורו
phrases.en: and it limits, therefore, the light of how far you can extend that kindness
the kindness limits, it opposes and limits the light of justice

blocks.text: The right line, *chachma*, *chesed*, *netzach*, is opposed by the left line, *bina*, *gevura*, *hod*. *Din* opposes *chesed*. If you only give, eventually *din* steps in, because kindness that enables harm has to stop. And *chesed* in turn limits the light of *din*.

So the opposite holds too: *chesed* limits the light of *din*. A person will say he only gives people what they deserve, but a baby cannot help himself, and a disabled person needs help. Even asking someone to pass the salt shows that at some point you simply have to be kind. You can't only be kind, and you can't only be harsh and judge. You need a limit.

phrases.en: eventually so it comes out that both of them stop
that's not called truth

phrases.he: כי עיקר האמת הוא מה שיש לו קיום,
phrases.en: the main idea of truth is something that's enduring
like it says in the verse, the lip of truth, true words will endure
but a lying, a false witness will be cut off
falseness is another word for *sheker*, which is *kazav*, deceit
that's related to the term *yichzevu mimav*
that's the idea that the river stops

blocks.text: If each side stops at its own extreme, both end up stopping, and that is not truth. A view that one should always be kind and never repay a wrong, turn the other cheek and that sort of thing, does not work when it is taken to the extreme.

blocks.title: Tit for tat in the game-theory simulations
blocks.text: In game-theory simulations of different strategies, the one that brings the most cooperation is neither pure kindness, which gets taken advantage of, nor pure meanness, which leaves everyone losing. The best is tit for tat: treat people the way they treat you, but now and then forgive, allow for making up, and show a little mercy. That makes the strategy work better even on a practical level.
This is more general. Truth is what is constant: it endures and transcends change, and that is why it is true. As the verse says, true lips will endure, and a false witness will be cut off.

*Sheker* is *kazav*, deceit, from the term *yichzevu mimav*, of a river whose waters lie. A river like the Nile or the Mississippi always flows, but a smaller river dries up in a dry year. Such a river's waters are not constant, and so it is not true.

phrases.he: ואמנם מדת האמת הוא המתקיים, להיותו כלול מב' הפכים
phrases.en: but the idea of truth is something that will endure, because it has both opposites
it's able to include and unite and harmonize both extremes, the *chesed* and *gevura* of kindness and justice
therefore there's nothing that opposes it because it has the balance of those two
therefore its water will not stop

blocks.text: Truth endures because it holds two opposites, *chesed* and *gevura*, and nothing opposes it, since it balances both. A thing that goes to one extreme fails and destroys itself. Balance and harmony let it continue.

blocks.title: The bicycle that balances itself
blocks.text: A stable system has a feedback loop: whatever pushes it off balance returns it to equilibrium. An unstable thing, pushed off, veers further and further. A bicycle is like that. Once it is moving it balances itself. You can roll one down a hill and it will steer itself, because it corrects itself. That is why it is easy to keep going once you are moving, while other things are very hard to balance.

phrases.en: this is what it means
the letter *vav* is the idea that it just goes straight down from the top to the bottom

phrases.he: קו האמצעי שכלול מחסד וגבורה, והוא דת''י (כמו שכתוב למעלה באות הכ''א)
phrases.en: that's the middle line, made up of both *chesed* and *gevura*, and that's the line of *daas*, *tiferes*, *yesod*, like we talked about previously in chapter 21

blocks.text: The *vav* is the middle line, and it goes straight from top to bottom with no kinks. It is made of *chesed* and *gevura*, and it is the line of *daas*, *tiferes*, *yesod*, as we discussed in chapter 21. That is one thing that makes the middle line special: it is balanced between *chesed* and *gevura*.

sections.title: The middle line runs unbroken from top to bottom
sections.summary: The middle line keeps its character from top to bottom, because it is one connected whole. The right and left lines are not joined in this way; they are connected only through the middle.

phrases.he: ועוד יש מעלה בקו האמצעי דת''י, שאין בו שינוי מראשו לסופו,
phrases.en: another advantage of the middle line is that it doesn't change from the top to the bottom

phrases.he: כי כמו שהוא בראש כך הוא בסוף
phrases.en: the way it is in the beginning stays the same in the end

phrases.he: ולא ישתנה מצד אריכות המשכתו למטה
phrases.en: it doesn't become diluted or changed from the process of being drawn down

phrases.he: והוא מצד חבור וקשר שיש בכולו, מראשו לסופו יחד כמהות א',
phrases.en: this is because it's completely connected from the top to the bottom

phrases.he: כבריח התיכון המבריח מן הקצה העליון לקצה התחתון
phrases.en: that it extends from the highest point all the way down to the lowest point

blocks.text: The middle line has one more advantage: it does not change from top to bottom. It is not only straight from right to left; as it goes down it does not change either. Its *sefiros* are like one thing, so it stays the same at the bottom, and being drawn down does not dilute it.

blocks.title: The beam from the top of the building to the bottom
blocks.text: A building may have one support beam from the top to the bottom. The beam in the *Mishkan* went all the way through the walls, from the highest point down to the lowest. In the body it is the spinal cord, from the head all the way to the bottom.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן ב' הקוין ימין ושמאל שאין בכל אחד מהם בחינת החיבור והקשר
phrases.en: in contrast, the two side lines, right and left, they're not connected

phrases.he: על כן לא ימצא בסופו כמו בראשו
phrases.en: the end is not going to be the same as it was in the beginning

blocks.title: The arms and legs, joined only through the trunk
blocks.text: The right and left lines are aligned but are not one thing. *Chachma* and *chesed* both lean to kindness, yet *chachma* does not go directly into *chesed*, just as the arms and legs extend from the body and are joined only through the trunk. So the end is not the same as the beginning.

sections.title: Netzach and hod: the middos lose their reason as they go down
sections.summary: As the middos go down to *netzach* and *hod*, the light of the *mochin* is cut off. The action remains, but it loses its reason and its commitment, and only a faint impression of the love is left.

phrases.he: כמו חח''ן, הרי בנצח יגרע אור השפע,
phrases.en: like the right line of *chachma*, *chesed*, *netzach*, by the time you get to *netzach* the light that's being given over becomes very diminished
and the same thing in *hod* on the left side
as is known

phrases.he: בענין נצח והוד שנקרא תרין בדי ערבות
phrases.en: that *netzach* and *hod* are called the two sticks of the *aravos*
they don't have any taste or smell

blocks.text: By the time the light reaches *netzach*, it is very diminished, and the same is true of *hod* on the left. *Netzach* and *hod* are the two willows of the *aravos*, which have no taste or smell. The taste is *sechel*, the reason, and the smell is the emotions. By *netzach* and *hod* both are gone.
A person does something simply because he has to: in a dry way, accepting the yoke, but not wanting to. He does it begrudgingly.

phrases.he: והוא מפני שנפסק בהן הארת המוחין,
phrases.en: and that's because they became detached from the *mochin*
even within one person *chesed* is only a branch of *chachma*

phrases.he: שהשכל והטעם שבחסד, כבר חלף ועבר עקרו
phrases.en: by the time the reason goes from *chachma* to *chesed*, the reason already is gone, mostly gone

phrases.he: ולא נשאר בו רק בצמצום והעלם
phrases.en: all that's left is just a very little hidden thing

blocks.text: Without the *mochin*, the middos lose the reason and purpose of what they do. A foot soldier who doesn't understand the strategy is only told to take the bridge, and he takes it. An employee who doesn't see the value of his work, and the big picture, does the minimum to avoid being fired and is not excited about it. He lacks the deeper, more mature perspective.

Intellectually I know I should do something, and I am angry about it. When people feel that anger they often forget the reason, the way you see in politics. By the time it comes to act, people may feel outrage, but don't take a stand, and it weakens.
That is why by the time it gets to *netzach* it loses that light. The reason of *chesed* is gone, mostly gone, and all that's left is a very little hidden thing.

phrases.en: so that reason that's motivating the feeling of *chesed* is still there
it's separate, it's detached from the feeling

phrases.he: ואין ביניהם חיבור וקשר כל כך
phrases.en: and they're not so connected

blocks.text: The reason is still there, hidden, and detached from the feeling, so they are not so connected. The inner purpose no longer has to be tied to the feeling, and people lose track. You see it in extremists: something sets them off, and they forget why they were doing it, because nothing tempers or balances it anymore.

phrases.en: this is the idea that we call *chesed* the right arm

phrases.he: כח היד ימין שנפסק מן המוח כו'
phrases.en: that's like the right arm, like we said that the power of the right arm is separate, it's not directly connected to the brain

blocks.text: The right arm stands for *chesed*. Its power is separate, not directly connected to the brain, like something coming out from the body: a little detached from the reason and purpose.

phrases.he: ובחינת הנצח שהוא ניצוח ההסכם לבד,
phrases.en: and then *netzach* is when a person is just going to have a commitment and determination to do something even though it's hard

phrases.he: כבר נפסק מן המוחין דחכמה יותר,
phrases.en: and then it becomes even more detached from the original reason

phrases.he: כי לא נשאר בו רק רושם בעלמא מן האהבה וחסד
phrases.en: there's only a little impression of the original reason and the original feeling, of that love and the kindness

blocks.text: *Netzach* is only the commitment, the determination to do something even when it is hard and you don't feel like it. It is detached further from the reason you first understood. A person keeps doing it and doesn't even know why. All that remains is a little impression of the love and the kindness.

phrases.he: והוא כמו הירך הימין שנפסק מחסד שביד ימין כו',
phrases.en: and that's like the right leg, which is detached, it's not directly connected to the right arm

phrases.he: ואין לירך חיבור עם היד כו'
phrases.en: and so the leg is not connected to the hand
and the same thing with the left hand
and the left leg
which is the left side of *bina*, *gevura*, *hod*
they are separate from each other

blocks.text: The right leg is detached from the *chesed* of the right hand, and a leg is not connected to a hand. So too the left hand and leg, the left line of *bina*, *gevura*, *hod*: separate.

Intellectually I know I should do something, and then I am angry about it. But when people feel that anger they often forget the reason, and it runs off, the way you see a lot in politics. By the time it comes to act, people may feel outrage, but they don't take a stand, and it gets weakened.

phrases.he: על כן בסופו לא ימצא מראשו, מפני הפסק הארת המוחין,
phrases.en: therefore, by the time it comes to the end of the actual actions that come from *netzach*

phrases.he: עד שיוכל להיות שם גרעון לגמרי,
phrases.en: to the point where you can have complete lack
and that's the idea that's symbolized when the angel

blocks.text: So at the end, the action that comes from *netzach* and *hod* does not keep the awareness and commitment it had at the start, because it is cut off from the *mochin* that motivates it. It can reach a complete lack, like *Yaakov*'s thigh, which the angel struck at *netzach*, in the *gid hanasheh*.
One explanation could be a failure in sexual matters. More generally, when we do right only because we know we should, the final action can weaken, and our instincts and bodily nature can take over.

It also means carrying on through children. A person may do something right, but his children may not continue it, and in a generation or two it gets eroded. That is the level of a person who does what is right because he knows it, without the deep understanding and feeling connected to what he does.

There will always be some lack or compromise in the subtle things if a person doesn't learn the inner aspects of *Torah*, like *Chassidus*. Doing it only because you're supposed to doesn't carry through, and you end up not even realizing that you are compromising in small areas.

The world today is so corrosive, in the media and in every aspect of life, that without a deep sense of who you are and why you do this, the truth won't carry through into everything you do, even the small things. Then you can't pass it to your children, because *chinuch* rests on *emes*. Children see that you don't really want to do it, and ask why they should. So a person on the level of *Yaakov*, not yet mature, is open to the *kelipa* taking hold of him, and that is the idea of the sciatic nerve.

sensitivity.reason: A sweeping jab at present-day culture and the media, not a group he names (STYLE, Softened: jabs at present-day cultures).
sensitivity.publishable: The world today is so pressing, in the media and in every aspect of life, that without a deep sense of who you are and why you do this, the truth won't carry through into everything you do, even the small things. Then you can't pass it to your children, because *chinuch* rests on *emes*. Children see that you don't really want to do it, and ask why they should. So a person on the level of *Yaakov*, not yet mature, is open to the *kelipa* taking hold of him, and that is the idea of the sciatic nerve.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: Whether the sweeping judgment of the present day (the media, every aspect of life) stays in print; the public text only softens the word.

sections.title: Lishma and the middle line: Yaakov stays joined from top to bottom
sections.summary: *Chesed* and *gevura* that are not joined to *chachma* and *bina* feed the outer forces, as *Yishmael* and *Esav* did. *Yaakov*, the middle line, stays connected from top to bottom, so even a sincere person on a low level can be plugged in to the truth.

phrases.en: was able to strike him on the level of *netzach*
in the *gid hanasheh*, the sciatic nerve
to the point where the *chitzonim* can receive nourishment from there

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בזהר בענין ירך סוטה
phrases.en: like the *Zohar* says about the thigh of the *sotah*

blocks.text: The outer forces can receive nourishment from that point: a person can be drawn into wrong, or use religion to justify it. The *Zohar* speaks of the thigh of the *sotah* in this sense: on this level there can be some impropriety in intimacy, and a desire for it.

blocks.title: Teenagers who lose their sense
blocks.text: The idea is that a person does not sin unless a spirit of foolishness enters him, and then he loses his *chachma*. Like kids and teenagers who do things that are just stupid: you say, what were you thinking? But they weren't thinking. They are used to following the rules, and once they get silly and start having fun, if they have no sense of what is right and wrong from inside them, they can quickly do things that are dangerous, ridiculous, or wrong.

sensitivity.reason: 'Stupid', said of what kids and teenagers do: an insult word applied to a group (STYLE, Sensitivity, insult words).
sensitivity.publishable: The idea is that a person does not sin unless a spirit of foolishness enters him, and then he loses his *chachma*. Like kids and teenagers who do things that are just foolish: you say, what were you thinking? But they weren't thinking. They are used to following the rules, and once they get silly and start having fun, if they have no sense of what is right and wrong from inside them, they can quickly do things that are dangerous, ridiculous, or wrong.

blocks.text: A person who functions only within nature, his animal soul and the nature of the world, and has no deeper awareness of where his priorities come from, does not change, and that is the sense of the Name. The deeper maturity is having things of intrinsic value: doing something *lishma*, wanting to know the truth because it is true and doing what is right because it is right. The *Rambam* describes a person on the level of *Yisroel* this way, when his soul is complete, with that inner conviction.
Even if *Yisroel* sins, he is still *Yisroel*: on that level he corrects it, because he knows what is right. Someone who does only what he is told, and feels it is not from him, is not there yet.

blocks.title: Prizes that lead to cheating
blocks.text: If you get a child to learn for the test and for prizes, the prize motivates him to cheat for a better grade. In sports that become very competitive, people lose the intrinsic motivation and are motivated only to win, so they cheat to win: steroids, weights in the bobsled, and other things like that.

When things are motivated from outside, that is the level of *Yaakov*: the real reason is disconnected from what you do. Bribes, prizes and rewards can connect them, but eventually that fails. It is the same with children: you have to reach the level of *Yisroel*, the sense that we do this because it is right. Rewards and celebrating success maybe help, but you are not doing the right thing because of them; you are doing it because this is who you are. Only a mature perspective gives consistency: it comes from inside, and the world can change while who I am does not.

If I am doing what is right because of something in the world, or because I want a reward, then when the circumstances change and the temptation gets strong enough, the calculus changes. Maybe it's not worth doing the right thing; maybe it's worth cheating a little and skimping once or twice, because you don't have integrity.

That is what they call selling your soul to the devil: giving up integrity and priorities to be successful. In a lot of industries that happens, and in music and in Hollywood they take advantage of people, put them where they must give up why they wanted to do this, and leave them trapped. Many end up really depressed, with problems, because they gave up themselves for something ultimately not important.

sensitivity.reason: Says that the music and film industries as a whole take advantage of people and leave them depressed: a sweeping remark about two professions.
sensitivity.publishable: That is what they call selling your soul to the devil: giving up integrity and priorities to be successful. In a lot of industries that happens; they take advantage of people, put them where they must give up why they wanted to do this, and leave them trapped. Many end up really depressed, with problems, because they gave up themselves for something ultimately not important.

blocks.text: The opposite of that is *shtus d'kedusha*: the sense that G-dly things, *Torah* and *mitzvos*, matter more, and that one can go against the winds of the world to keep them. That integrity is the idea of *Yisroel*. Now one has to be crazy to stand against the world, because the corrosion of values is everywhere, and you cannot defend yourself only rationally and still stay part of society.

sensitivity.reason: A sweeping jab at present-day culture: the corrosion of values is everywhere (STYLE, Softened: jabs at present-day cultures).
sensitivity.publishable: The opposite of that is *shtus d'kedusha*: the sense that G-dly things, *Torah* and *mitzvos*, matter more, and that one can go against the winds of the world to keep them. That integrity is the idea of *Yisroel*. Now one has to be crazy to stand against the world, because the pressure on values is everywhere, and you cannot defend yourself only rationally and still stay part of society.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: Whether the sweeping judgment of the present day stays in print, as in the block before it; the public text only softens the word.

blocks.text: This is a big part of the Rebbe's teaching: *Yaakov* and *Yisroel* are the foundation of the teachings on *chinuch*, because its essence is *emes*.

Even though we use extrinsic things with a child to help him mature, we always have to imbue it, even for a little child, with the deeper perspective of *emes*. You should do it because it is right and it is your responsibility, whether you like it or not; but to make it easier, I'll reward you or motivate you with a carrot and a stick. That subtle difference is what makes it *emes*, and it is what makes it real. It is the Yiddish saying that *Torah* is the best merchandise. *Shabbos* is supposed to connect to exactly this *emes* and this intrinsic value, and we will talk more about *Shabbos* later, I think.

phrases.he: והיינו הטעם גם כן בחסד וגבורה עצמן,
phrases.en: and you have a similar problem even in *chesed* and *gevura*

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב אברהם יצא ממנו ישמעאל,
phrases.en: and like we see that *Avraham*, who is the idea of *chesed*, but *Yishmael* came out from him
which is the idea that just pure just being kind can lead to a negative type of kindness, that is kindness, but it's self-centered and it can feed

phrases.he: ויצחק יצא ממנו עשו, מותרי ופסולת הגבורות כו'
phrases.en: and *Yitzchak* had *Esav*, so the harshness of *Yitzchak* led to *Esav*

blocks.text: The same problem is in *chesed* and *gevura*: without full connection to *chachma* and *bina*, the outer forces can be fed.
*Avraham* was *chesed*, yet *Yishmael* came out from him. That is the waste of *chesed*: a kindness that is self-centered, that can feed the ego, and that ends up destructive.
*Yitzchak* was *gevura*, and *Esav* came out of him: so hard on himself that he gave up trying to be good, feeling he was never good enough. He was also a murderer. That is the waste of *gevura*.

phrases.he: אבל יעקב שהוא בחינת קו האמצעי
phrases.en: but *Yaakov*, he is the middle line

phrases.he: הרי יש בקו זה חיבור וקשר מראשו לסופו,
phrases.en: so that's fully connected from the top to the bottom

phrases.he: עד שימצא בסופו כמו בראשו ממש

blocks.text: *Yaakov* is the middle line of *daas*, *tiferes*, *yesod*, connected from top to bottom, so the end is the same as the beginning. All his children followed his ways: successful *chinuch* that comes from *emes*. That is why the tribes said to him, *Shema Yisroel*: we believe in G-d just as you do, though we are on a lower level, with the same faith.
As is known, *yesod* is connected to *daas*: a man cannot have an erection without *daas*, even in *halacha*.

And so in *halacha*, this is the idea that a man can't claim rape the same way a woman can in certain situations, and it's a debate, exactly, but it's not the same, because a man can't be totally passive. That is the idea that *yesod* has to be connected to the *daas* in the head.

sensitivity.reason: Gives a halachic rule about men's and women's claims of rape, and a remark on men's passivity, as his own point; a public reader could take it as a ruling on a sensitive matter, and the halacha is not in the cited words.
sensitivity.publishable: And so in *halacha*, this is the idea that *yesod* has to be connected to the *daas* in the head.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: Whether his halachic point about claims of rape stays in print at all, or is cut as in the publishable text; it needs a check against the halacha he means.

blocks.text: The *Mitteler Rebbe* has a whole *maamar* on this. The Gemara asks why *talmidei chachamim* have children who are *am ha'aretz*, and answers that they call the ignorant donkeys. He explains that *yesod*, which is reproduction and spiritually having children who follow your values, requires seeing the value in someone lower than you. Without that deeper truth you cannot pass it down, even to your own children.
So you have to have that deeper *emes* to have the *middah* of *yesod*. This is the point he made back in what he thinks was chapter 21: it takes a deeper *chacham* to explain things simply.

blocks.question: Before, *Yaakov* represented immaturity and *Yisroel* maturity. Here *Yaakov* is the middle line, which seems mature. How is that?
blocks.text: In the middle line, even *Yaakov*'s immature perspective connects up to *Yisroel*, which the right and left lines do not: that is why *Avraham* went down to *Yishmael*. Even at a low level, *kabbalas ol* has a truth that goes all the way down.

Every person can be like what the *Alter Rebbe* explains in *Tanya*: you can have what is true on your level. You may be far below a *tzaddik*, but for where you are, you are doing what is true. *Yaakov* represents that sincerity, which is why he was called a *tam*. Even on a very low level, sincerity connects all the way up to the truth of a *tzaddik*, so one can be immature and still be in the middle line.

The *Alter Rebbe* in the *Kuntres HaHispaalus* speaks of many levels of *avodah*, from *nefesh* to *yechida*; as long as you turn on the *nefesh Elokis* and do what is real for your level, that is perfect. A sincere person will peel potatoes for the *farbrengen* if that has to get done, or chop wood if G-d wants, even at the lowest level of simple faith.

In *Tanya* he speaks of the levels of *tzaddik*, *rasha* and *beinoni*, but the main thing is whether a person is serving G-d or not, and whether he is turned on and working to grow and improve. Whatever your level, you need to be turned on and growing and improving, and that is the real *avodah*. So that is the idea of *Yaakov* as the middle line.

sections.title: Daas: the inner part of rachamim, and the connection of yesod
sections.summary: *Daas* is the inner part of *rachamim*: a person without *daas* is cruel, and as *daas* grows, mercy grows with it. The same middle line joins *yesod* to *daas*, and in education it means seeing what each person needs.

phrases.he: (כמו שידוע, דאין קישוי אלא לדעת שבראש, הרי קשור בחינת היסוד בדעת שבמוח הראש, כאילו הן מהות אחת כו')
phrases.en: and so *yesod* is connected with the *daas* that's in the mind, as if they're one thing

blocks.text: *Yesod* is connected to the *daas* in the head as if they were one thread, represented by the spinal column that connects everything in the middle.

phrases.en: that the inner *daas* is the idea of being able to see, take things personally, see how things relate to you
that is really the essence of *rachamim* in the heart
and therefore they're always one

blocks.text: *Daas* is the inner part of the middos: seeing how things relate to you. That is the essence of *rachamim*.

blocks.title: Yaakov with his children
blocks.text: *Yaakov* looked at each child and saw what he needed, and saw himself in them. *Avraham* did everything with *chesed*, but *Yishmael* needed *gevura*. *Yitzchak* did everything with *gevura*, but *Esav* needed *chesed*. *Yaakov* could balance *chesed* and *gevura* according to what the person needed, and that comes from *daas*: understanding the person and seeing where he is.
Without *daas* there is no empathy: lose the ability to put yourself in the other's shoes, and you stop feeling for him.

phrases.he: וכמו שאמר בזהר, משה מלגאו יעקב מלבר
phrases.en: that *Moshe* is the inner, and *Yaakov* is on the outside

phrases.he: והוא בחינת הדעת, שהוא פנימיות המדות של הרחמים
phrases.en: so *daas* is the inner part of *rachamim*

phrases.he: כי לפי ערך הדעת, ממש כך ערך הרחמים
phrases.en: like you see that according to a person's *daas*, that's how much mercy they're going to have

blocks.text: The *Zohar* says *Moshe* is inside and *Yaakov* outside: *Moshe* is *daas*, *Yaakov* is *tiferes*, *rachamim*, so *daas* is the inner part of *rachamim*. As the *daas* is, so is the *rachamim*.

phrases.he: וכל מי שאין בו דעת הוא אכזרי, כתינוק וכהאי גוונא,
phrases.en: and somebody doesn't have *daas*, is cruel, like a small child
and the more a person increases their *daas*, the more they're going to feel pity for the person

blocks.text: Without *daas* a person is cruel, like a small child who hurts animals or fights, not thinking how the other feels. More *daas* brings more mercy.

That is why it matters to teach a child manners. Instead of "I'm thirsty, give me water," he learns to say, "Mommy, could you please pass me the water?" That small effort makes him recognize the other person and think about how they feel. You train that awareness right away, and you have to listen to the person and care about him.

When he worked with teenagers in a yeshiva, he used a method that goes back to *emes*. First lay out the facts, without emotion: what happened. That is the *din* side. Then switch to what the person was feeling and what his valid need was, and validate it: that need is totally valid. Then bring the two together: this strategy is not appropriate, you crossed a line, so next time find something else.

Then set the boundaries: say what will happen if you do it the right way and what will happen if you do it the wrong way. I'm here to help you and coach you, but I'm also here to set limits and, if I need to, reward and punishment, so that you don't cross those lines. Those kids were usually sent to him as trouble, and they always left feeling good, because they felt heard and understood.

Some approaches are too much *chesed*, with no boundaries and no demands on the child: you have responsibilities, some things are totally unacceptable, and we won't tolerate them. You need both sides. Putting them together makes the person feel good, because you believe in him and want him to succeed and learn the boundaries. It requires understanding the person too.

blocks.title: Montessori and one part of the truth
blocks.text: Montessori methods may be done with too much *chesed*, and he thinks it depends who is doing it. Someone asked the Rebbe about doing Montessori things, and the Rebbe said it is good to go and learn from it, but you shouldn't get too into the philosophy. I think the idea is that outside methods take one part of the truth and try to make it everything. In Torah, the general principles of *chinuch* taught by the *Frierdiker Rebbe* show how all these things fit together.

A child who lacks *daas* is cruel, and the more *daas* a person has, the more he feels pity. He cannot just be detached and lay down the law. You can empathize: you could see yourself doing what they did in their circumstances, and you wouldn't have been any better. So you want to help the person too. What they did is wrong, but you see how they came to it, and you understand what it takes to get them out.

phrases.en: as explained elsewhere at length

phrases.he: שאין בין הדעת והרחמים שום הפסק כלל,
phrases.en: there's no break, there's no interruption between *daas* and *rachamim*

phrases.he: כמו בין החכמה וחסד הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: unlike the break between *chachma* and *chesed*

blocks.text: This is explained elsewhere at length: there is no break between *daas* and *rachamim*; it is the same essence in a new arena. That is the middle line: always the same truth, applied in different areas. The *yechida* can be expressed on different levels, according to one's *avodah*, but always plugs into the same truth.

*Chachma* is the perspective that sees beyond distinctions: we all seem the same, so you should be kind to everybody. That's basically the liberal philosophy: you shouldn't judge people by these differences, and that leads to wanting to be kind. There is truth to that.

sensitivity.reason: Names a political label, the liberal philosophy, as the doctrine he is describing; the word is his, the point is about how one sees people.
sensitivity.publishable: *Chachma* is the perspective that sees beyond distinctions: we all seem the same, so you should be kind to everybody. That's basically the philosophy: you shouldn't judge people by these differences, and that leads to wanting to be kind. There is truth to that.

blocks.text: There is truth in that, but some differences matter: whether a person is a criminal, and his education and circumstances. So modulate your response to how he acts and to his situation.

That truth of *chachma* goes into *daas* and into the middle line, but it is only part. You also have to recognize the differences in a person's situation: essentially we are all the same, but practically we are very different. Being treated the same just because, philosophically, we're all the same is dehumanizing. Truth and mercy come from understanding both sides and putting them together, to help the person.

phrases.he: ומכל שכן החיבור אל השפעת היסוד, שהוא בחינת התקשרות המשפיע אל המקבל
phrases.en: even stronger when you go down to *yesod*, where the *mashpia* is connecting to the *mekabel*
that when *Adam* was intimate with *Chavah*, it says that he knew her

blocks.text: The connection at *yesod* is stronger still: the one who influences is joined to the one who receives, as when a person teaches or helps someone. That matters more than the emotions, which only process it, because the goal is to have an impact. That is why it says *Adam knew Chavah*: the mental connection is focused on, and expressed in, the physical one, and the two become one.

phrases.en: and there's also the *netzach*, *hod*, *yesod* within the inner
that's the kidneys that give advice
and the inner of *yesod*, which is that it's the end of the body

phrases.he: ונו"ה בחיצוניות הן תרין ירכין כו׳)
phrases.en: and then the outer is the arms and the legs, those are the outer of *chesed* and *gevura*, *netzach* and *hod*

blocks.text: Why does the text use *daas* for the physical act? Because intimacy is also a deep mental and spiritual connection: a person feels a bond with the other and wants to become one with them, and to have a child with them. It goes beyond the ego, because who we are is not just me as a man or me as a woman. *Reishis Chochma* explains this at length, and other commentators too.

*Netzach*, *hod* and *yesod* are also inner, like the kidneys that give counsel, and *yesod* is the end of the body. All the *sefiros* are as they are in the middle line, in the inner part: that is the *partzuf* of *Yaakov* and *Yisroel*. The organs are inner; the arms and legs are the outer of *chesed* and *gevura*, *netzach* and *hod*.

sections.title: Yaakov did not die: the middle line, emes, and the root of Yaakov
sections.summary: The middle line is where the *kelipos* have no grip: *Yaakov* did not die, because his inner middos are joined to *daas* and *chachma*. *Emes* is the middle line of the alphabet, the letters from the beginning to the end, and *Yisroel* rules over nature from the head.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב בזהר בראשית, בענין יקוו המים כו' אל מקום אחד,
phrases.en: like it's explained in the *Zohar* about the waters being gathered, that G-d gathered all the waters into the ocean, to one place

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת יסוד שמתקבץ שם כל השפע,
phrases.en: that's the gathering of all the lights of all the *sefiros*
and that's called the collection, the gathering place of all the lights

blocks.text: The *Zohar* says that the waters were gathered into one place: that is *yesod*, which gathers all the *shefa*, and it is called the gathering place of all the lights. In reproduction, the connection of the *middah* of *yesod* gathers all the lights of the *sefiros*.

In reproduction you give over the essence of life, so the child becomes independent. A good teacher gives the inner truth of how to think and learn. Real education is not telling someone what to do because he was told, but giving him the essence, so he becomes a mature adult who makes his own judgments.

phrases.en: that's the idea of the middle line that goes from the top all the way to the bottom

blocks.text: The middle line goes from the top to the bottom, imbuing the bottom with everything from the top.

phrases.en: and that's why it's called *emes*

phrases.he: שהן אותיות א' מ' ת' ראש תוך סוף
phrases.en: in the Hebrew alphabet is the first letter, the middle letter, and the last letter, the beginning, middle, and end
the idea of *emes* is that from the beginning to the middle to the end, it's all connected, it's all the same
that's the main idea of truth, right, that doesn't change

blocks.text: *Emes* is spelled with *aleph*, *mem*, *tav*, the first, middle and last letters: beginning, middle and end, all connected and the same. *Sheker* is made of letters next to each other in the alphabet, and in reverse order too, with many hints. The base of *emes* is wide, combining *chesed* and *gevura*, so it has something to stand on. The letters of *sheker* come to one point, one extreme or the other, so it cannot last.

phrases.he: ולזה אמרו יעקב לא מת כו',
phrases.en: and therefore it says, *Yaakov* didn't die

phrases.he: מפני שאין אחיזה למות, שרש הקליפות, בקו האמצעי כלל,
phrases.en: because there's no way for the *kelipa* to grab onto the middle line

blocks.text: The simple meaning is that his children perfectly carry over who he is, so he continues to live on through them. *Avraham* and *Yitzchak* were a little extreme. *Avraham* blazed a new path, but not every person can be an *Avraham*: to blow up society and go against everything is not sustainable, and sometimes you have to be like that, but *Yaakov* was the family man, and everybody can be him.

blocks.question: *Avraham* was supposed to be a person of *chesed*, but he smashed the idols?
blocks.text: I think he definitely had some *gevura*. *Avraham* and *Yitzchak* were correct for themselves, but could not bring it fully to their children and others the way *Yaakov* did. That is why *Yaakov* started something eternal, the Jewish people.
The *kelipa* could reach *Yaakov* only on his leg, the outer. The inner of the middle line it could not reach, and *Yaakov* is that inner part.

blocks.question: Does it mean that *Yaakov* is walking around, since it says he didn't die?
blocks.text: No. The *Gemara* says they embalmed and buried him. The physical part, which the Egyptians related to, died and was buried. But *Yaakov* was not the body: his beliefs and ideals were given over perfectly to his children.

If my identity is external, my children won't carry it on. If it is something true beyond my personality and circumstances, they can carry it perfectly, and I live on through them. That is why *Yaakov* did not die.

blocks.title: Eliyahu at the brit and at the Idra
blocks.text: *Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi* comes back to make *kiddush* for his family. *Eliyahu* comes to a *brit* spiritually, so he can be in many places at once. But once in the *Zohar* he did not come to the *Idra*, because he had to rescue *Rav Hamnuna Saba* in his body. That is a whole *sugya*, not for now.

phrases.he: ולזה אמר כי שרית עם אלהי״ם,
phrases.en: and therefore it says, that you ruled over *Elokim*
that inner g-dly sense, that's ruling over my outer, external, like my body and my physical nature

blocks.text: The simple meaning is that he ruled over angels; the idea is that he ruled over nature, the outer. The inner G-dly sense of who I am, the *nefesh Elokis*, rules over my body and animal soul. That is *Elokim*: G-d transcends nature and rules over it.

phrases.he: והוא בבחינת הדעת והחכמה בראש דישראל, לי ראש דוקא
phrases.en: and this ability to rule over nature really comes from the *daas* and *chachma* in the head
like we said, that even a person on the level of *Yaakov* can have that in an immature way

phrases.he: ולכך אמר לו ישראל יהיה שמך
phrases.en: therefore, he was told that *Yisroel* will be your name

blocks.text: *Yisroel* is *li rosh*, I have a head: ruling over nature comes from *daas* and *chachma* in the head, the awareness that makes a *Yisroel*. A person on the level of *Yaakov* has it in an immature way, not yet revealed, so he can overcome his nature. That is why his name was to be *Yisroel*: his inner was this *daas* and *chachma*, which he fully revealed.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן יעקב מצד בחינת חיצוניות דנצח והוד, תרין ירכין כו'
phrases.en: but the way *Yaakov* was on the outer level, in his inner, *Yaakov* is really *Yisroel*, which rules over nature

phrases.he: שבאין מכחו של חסד וגבורה דאברהם ויצחק כו'
phrases.en: in his outer there can be a *yenika* of the *chitzonim*

blocks.text: The outer of *Yaakov*, *netzach* and *hod*, comes from *Avraham*'s and *Yitzchak*'s *chesed* and *gevura*, so the outer forces can feed there. That is why the angel could touch the thigh, in the *netzach* of the right line.
The inner of *netzach* is giving over to one's children, to remain strong. Its outer is what the angel could harm.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בישראל נאמר וגם נצח ישראל לא ישקר כו'
phrases.en: that's why it says *netzach* of *Yisroel* cannot lie

blocks.text: *Yaakov*'s inner is always good, as the *Tanya* says: what is near to you is very near. Reveal it and you can overcome everything, and that never changes. For *Yaakov* the outer is not always revealed; at the level of *Yisroel* it is, and the outer cannot be affected. That is why it says the *netzach* of *Yisroel* cannot lie.

blocks.text: Having that awareness, from learning the inner part of *Torah*, lets a person rule his nature, the mind ruling the heart. As we said before, at twenty a person can change what he wants and enjoys, which is why we only let a person go to war at twenty: he can keep control of his instincts in a trying time. That comes from *Yisroel*.

*Yaakov* did not die because it says a person dies, but not with *chachma*. Connected to *chachma* he does not die. *Mat* (dead) is *emes* without the *alef*, the head; lose the head and you are left with the outer, which can become *mat*.

We can do things with no *chayus*. *Chassidus* gives life through understanding, connecting us to our *emuna* and revealing it. Everybody has *emuna* on the level of *Yaakov*; bring it into *sechel*, and it reaches *Yisroel* and shines even in the outer. That is the whole point of learning *Chassidus*.

and that's higher than the chest

phrases.en: and this is because *Yaakov*'s source really goes all the way up

blocks.text: The Sages say that *Yaakov* is still serving above in heaven. He connects to *chachma* and *bina*, since *daas* is great and goes up above the chest. The middos of *Yaakov* in the chest are *tiferes*, but their root goes up, to *chachma* and *bina*, and that is the level of *Yisroel*, as explained elsewhere.

*Yaakov*'s source goes all the way up: *tiferes* to *daas* to *chachma* and *bina*. But his outer middos, where he touched the hollow of his thigh, can have a *yenika* of the *kelipa*, as explained elsewhere.

The middle line is superior: it balances right and left and joins top to bottom. Revealed, its inner is the level of *Yisroel*, with no *yenika* even in the outer; unrevealed, the outer of *Yaakov* can be harmed.

I think the *nimshal* is our *avodah*: with a less mature perspective the outer can be in *galus*, but the soul of a Jew is never in *galus*, only the body. When the mature perspective is revealed, it brings the *geulah* even physically.
So, on a simple level, when we have *shtus d'kedusha*, eventually that brings the *geulah*, even in the outer.

reviewQuestions.question: How do *Yisroel* and *Yaakov* differ, and what does the name *Yisroel* mean in *Kabbalah*?
Why does the middle line stay joined from top to bottom when the right and left lines are not?
Why do *netzach* and *hod* lose their reason, and what do the foot soldier and the employee show?
What does the *Zohar* mean by the letter of truth, and what do the letters of *emes* teach?
How is *daas* related to *rachamim*, and why is a person without *daas* cruel?
